title: ‘Declare state of calamity for El Niño early’
summary: A state of calamity should be declared early enough by the government in provinces most likely to bear the brunt of the anticipated super El Niño, a minority leader has said.

blocks.text: In her House Resolution 1629, Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima underscored the urgency of the matter, pursuant to the “Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010 (RA 10121)” for the implementation of remedial measures, among others.
MANILA, Philippines — A state of calamity should be declared early enough by the government in provinces most likely to bear the brunt of the anticipated super El Niño, a minority leader has said.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council should make a recommendation, she said.

De Lima urged the declaration of a State of Imminent Disaster in areas forecast to face severe impacts of El Niño, to enable timely interventions and effective preventive response to avoid and mitigate potential damage.

At the same time, the House leadership also called on the Department of Agriculture to fast-track the release of the remaining P14 billion unspent government funds for 2026 to combat the looming El Niño phenomenon.
“We really have to be prepared for the eventuality of this super El Niño that we will be facing,” Rep. Mark Enverga said.
